summary: The bill amends the tax code to create an above-the-line deduction for qualified flood insurance premiums (including NFIP and private policies) paid by individuals on their property, but only for taxpayers with adjusted gross income below $200,000 ($400,000 for joint returns).

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a new tax deduction but does not authorize or appropriate any direct government outlays or program expansions. It operates entirely through the tax code rather than spending legislation, so it has no bearing on government spending levels.

The core provision adds an above-the-line deduction for qualified flood insurance premiums (both NFIP and private), directly reducing taxable income for eligible taxpayers up to the $200k/$400k AGI cap. This is a targeted tax reduction, producing a clear positive effect on the taxation scale.
No provisions address health insurance, medical care delivery, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions affect military budgets, defense programs, or related spending.
While flood insurance relates indirectly to climate-driven flooding risks, the bill only adjusts tax treatment of premiums and does not alter environmental regulations, protections, or enforcement.
The deduction is not a welfare, entitlement, or means-tested benefit expansion; it is a tax-code adjustment available only to those who purchase flood insurance and meet the income cap.
No provisions address schools, school choice, federal education funding, or related policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related matters.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.

By reducing federal revenue through a new deduction, the bill marginally increases the deficit relative to current law. This runs counter to prioritizing debt reduction, though the effect is modest and indirect.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, election integrity, or related reforms.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer flexibility.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.

The bill creates a new above-the-line deduction for flood insurance premiums, directly reducing federal tax revenue with no offsetting revenue raisers or spending cuts. The entire legislation is devoted to this tax relief measure.
